title: Divisibility by the equations of distinct hyperplanes
statement: Let $k$ be an infinite field [def-weil-field], and let $r,m,d\geq0$ be integers. Put $R=k[x_1,\ldots,x_r]$ [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring]. Let $\ell_1,\ldots,\ell_m\in R$ be nonzero homogeneous linear polynomials, no two proportional by a nonzero scalar in $k$. For every $P\in R$ satisfying $P(a)=0$ for every $i$ and every $a\in k^r$ with $\ell_i(a)=0$, one has $\prod_{i=1}^m\ell_i\mid P$. This product is nonzero. If, in addition, $P$ is homogeneous of degree $d$ (every monomial with nonzero coefficient has total degree $d$, allowing $P=0$), then $P=0$ when $d<m$, and $P=c\prod_{i=1}^m\ell_i$ for some $c\in k$ when $d=m$. The empty family of linear polynomials is allowed.

source.place: Tag 0BC1, lemma-polynomial-ring-UFD: factoriality input for the agent-formulated hyperplane-divisibility corollary. The coordinate restriction and homogeneity argument is given in the worker report; the corollary is not claimed to be the verbatim Stacks statement.

proof.text: Write $D_j=\prod_{i=1}^j\ell_i$, with $D_0=1$. By [lem-sfb-polynomial-field-ufd] the polynomial ring over $k$, in any finite number of variables including zero, is a domain. Thus every $D_j$ is nonzero, inductively: $D_0=1\ne0$, and multiplication of two nonzero elements cannot be zero. If $r=0$, no nonzero homogeneous linear polynomial exists, so $m=0$. In this case the divisibility conclusion is $1\mid P$, and a homogeneous polynomial of degree zero is a scalar; a polynomial homogeneous of positive degree in zero variables is zero. We may henceforth take $r>0$.

proof.text:
Fix any nonzero linear form $\ell=\sum_t a_tx_t$. Choose $j$ with $a_j
e0$, set $A=k[x_t:t
e j]$ and $b=-a_j^{-1}\sum_{t
e j}a_tx_t\in A$. For $F\in R$, let $\overline F\in A$ denote substitution $x_j=b$. From the monomial expansion in [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring], write $F=\sum_{n\ge0}c_nx_j^n$ with finitely many $c_n\in A$. The identity $x_j^n-b^n=(x_j-b)\sum_{s=0}^{n-1}x_j^{n-1-s}b^s$ for $n\ge1$ gives $F-\overline F=(x_j-b)T$ for an explicit finite sum $T\in R$. Since $\ell=a_j(x_j-b)$, this proves $\overline F=0\Longleftrightarrow\ell\mid F$; the reverse implication is substitution in a product. If $F$ vanishes at every $k$-point of $\ell=0$, then $\overline F$ evaluates to zero on every assignment of the remaining variables, since those assignments together with $x_j=b$ give such points. Apply [lem-sfb-mvpolynomial-infinite-evaluation] to $\overline F$ and zero to obtain $\overline F=0$. This works also when $r=1$, where $A=k$.

source.place: Tag 0BC1, lemma-polynomial-ring-UFD, field-domain input; agent hyperplane argument (not a proof attributed to Stacks)

proof.text:
Induct on $j$ to construct $Q_j$ with $P=D_jQ_j$. For $j=0$ take $Q_0=P$. Suppose $j<m$ and such $Q_j$ is given. Use the substitution in the preceding step for $\ell=\ell_{j+1}$. For every $i\le j$, $\overline{\ell_i}$ is a homogeneous linear polynomial in the remaining variables and is nonzero: if $\ell_i=\sum_t c_tx_t$ restricted to zero, its coefficient at $x_t$ for $t
e j_0$ would give $c_t=c_{j_0}a_t/a_{j_0}$, where $j_0$ is the chosen coordinate for $\ell_{j+1}$. Consequently $\ell_i=(c_{j_0}/a_{j_0})\ell_{j+1}$; the scalar cannot be zero since $\ell_i
e0$, contradicting nonproportionality. The remaining-variable polynomial ring is a domain by [lem-sfb-polynomial-field-ufd], so $\overline{D_j}=\prod_{i\le j}\overline{\ell_i}
e0$, including $j=0$. The vanishing hypothesis and the preceding step give $\overline P=0$. Substituting in $P=D_jQ_j$ yields $0=\overline{D_j}\,\overline{Q_j}$, whence $\overline{Q_j}=0$. The explicit identity of the preceding step now gives $Q_j=\ell_{j+1}Q_{j+1}$. Thus $P=D_{j+1}Q_{j+1}$. At $j=m$ this proves the asserted divisibility.

source.place: Tag 0BC1, lemma-polynomial-ring-UFD, field-domain input; agent hyperplane argument (not a proof attributed to Stacks)

proof.text: Assume now that $P$ is homogeneous of degree $d$. If $P=0$, both conclusions hold, with scalar $c=0$ when $d=m$. Otherwise write $P=D_mQ$ by the induction; $Q\ne0$ because $P\ne0$. Each $\ell_i$ has total degree one, directly from its nonzero linear coefficient support. Repeated application of [lem-sfb-mvpolynomial-total-degree-product] to the nonzero prefix products gives $\operatorname{tdeg}(D_m)=m$, starting from $\operatorname{tdeg}(1)=0$. A nonzero homogeneous polynomial of degree $d$ has total degree $d$, since its support is nonempty and all exponent sums are $d$. Applying the same cited statement to $P=D_mQ$ gives $d=m+\operatorname{tdeg}(Q)\ge m$. Thus $d<m$ forces $P=0$. If $d=m$, then $\operatorname{tdeg}(Q)=0$, so every monomial of $Q$ has exponent sum zero, hence every exponent zero. Thus $Q=c\in k$ and $P=cD_m$. The argument includes $m=0$, where $D_m=1$.
